narration: The evidence also needs context. A recent trend can describe what happened, but it cannot promise what happens next. Park and matchup information may change the environment, but not the final outcome. Market-implied context is not true probability. And one strong signal should not erase late lineup news, role changes, weather, or a moved line.

narration: Then separate direction from confidence. Direction answers which side the combined evidence supports. Confidence answers how strongly the model supports that side for the displayed line. Neither one tells you the payout, entry correlation, or whether PrizePicks currently offers that exact projection.

narration: A cheat sheet cannot establish that the player is active, the line is unchanged, the projection is available in your location, the entry terms are favorable, or the outcome will hit. It also cannot replace the final screen inside PrizePicks.

So use this checklist. Confirm the player. Confirm the stat. Read the exact line. Check the timestamp. Inspect the supporting evidence and missing inputs. Read direction and confidence separately. Then verify the actual PrizePicks projection before making your own decision.
